newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Speedpost to have tracking system for express mail.
newsitem.headline: Speedpost to have tracking system for express mail.

text.p: The Hong Kong post office is planning to introduce the first stage of a HK$10.4 million track and trace system to its Speedpost express mail delivery division later this year, senior Speedpost official Aubrey Au said.
Speedpost is a major air cargo user with many of its 4 million express items in and out of Hong Kong each year travelling as belly cargo on scheduled carriers to 80 countries world-wide.

Speedpost customers can expect to take advantage of the new tracking system from September, Au said in an interview. Customers will also be able to follow other post office products such as registered mail, parcels and recorded delivery items as the rest of the system is introduced.
Rival courier companies have already introduced package tracking systems and the post office was responding to the intense competition in the Hong Kong market, Au said.
"Customers should be able to track and trace from the acceptance point to the delivery point via telephone. We're also exploring whether it could be used through the Internet," she said.
